classification.difficultyReason: Constructs an auxiliary triangle with three known sides, uses the cosine rule to determine its angle and obtains the trapezium area from the resulting height.

inlines.text: The following shows a trapezium with parallel sides with lengths 5 cm and 11 cm. The other two sides are 3 cm and 5 cm.
Find the area of the trapezium in square centimetres, correct to one decimal place.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13 trapezium between the stem and final instruction
spec.description: Unshaded trapezium with A upper left, D upper right, B lower left and C lower right. Both upper vertices lie inside the lower base endpoints.
spec.mathematics: AD∥BC; AD=5 cm, BC=11 cm, AB=3 cm and DC=5 cm. Coordinates satisfy all four side lengths. No height, auxiliary construction or additional mark is student-visible.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the printed givens and vertex labels are visible.

answer.short:
$20.0\text{ cm}^2$.

Construct $DE\parallel AB$ with $E$ on $BC$; the cosine rule gives the height $\frac{2\sqrt{14}}{3}$ cm.
answer.worked:
Draw $DE\parallel AB$, with $E$ on $BC$. Since $ABED$ is a parallelogram, $BE=5$ cm, $DE=3$ cm and $EC=6$ cm.

Let $\phi=\angle DEC$ and let $h$ be the perpendicular height.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\phi&=\frac{3^2+6^2-5^2}{2(3)(6)}\\\cos\phi&=\frac59\\\sin\phi&=\sqrt{1-\left(\frac59\right)^2}\\\sin\phi&=\frac{2\sqrt{14}}9\\h&=3\sin\phi\\h&=\frac{2\sqrt{14}}3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Thus
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12(5+11)\left(\frac{2\sqrt{14}}3\right)\\\text{Area}&=\frac{16\sqrt{14}}3\text{ cm}^2\\\text{Area}&\approx20.0\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
